propositions: The LLM judge exhibits stochastic drift in per-finding Pass-2 decisions across repeated runs, introducing noise into sub-answer vocabulary (e.g., R5's asserted_capability_confirmed).
The gate verdict outcome flips across section-order permutations of the same plan, violating order-independence required for stable criteria routing.

Experiment A measures self-consistency of decisions over N=50 findings from the G6/E4/T3 cohort via 3-vote Fleiss kappa and raw agreement, requiring both kappa>=0.6 and raw_agreement>=0.8 to unblock R5.

Experiment B measures order-shuffle stability of verdicts over 14 plans with >=3 top-level sections via 3 deterministic permutations, requiring both kappa>=0.6 and raw_agreement>=0.8 as an R3 prerequisite.

Infrastructure-induced INDETERMINATEs (marked by coverage.llm_unavailable or coverage.verify_failed flags) are excluded and re-run; genuine judge INDETERMINATEs are retained as a valid agreement category.

The test produces committed frozen inputs (e6_selfconsistency_inputs.jsonl, e6_ordershuffle_inputs.jsonl) and agreement tables (e6_selfconsistency_agreement.csv, e6_ordershuffle_agreement.csv) with summary metrics in e6_summary.json, enabling reproducibility without re-running the LLM judge.
